summary: The paper measures a known one-pass out-of-fold filter (drop samples whose cross-validated logistic regression prediction disagrees with the given label, then refit) on digits and breast cancer with clean labels and two rates of symmetric noise over 5 seeds. It shows that under noise most dropped samples are mislabeled, that the refit model has a higher mean accuracy than unfiltered logistic regression in every noisy setting (not significantly on breast cancer at the lower rate) but stays below clean-label training, and that the cost on clean labels is small.
strengths: The main claims are scoped carefully. The paper states that it proposes no new method, reports the non-significant gain on breast cancer at the lower rate, names a weak case, and says which controls were not run.

The comparison with unfiltered logistic regression is paired and fair in its mechanics: shared splits and noisy labels, standardization refit inside every fold and before the final fit, the same C, and clean test labels. The method text matches experiments/run.py.

Judging the filter against known flips is informative. Drop precision, drop recall, the mislabeled share of the kept set and the share of correct samples lost are all reported, and the analytic random-removal reference in Sec. 4.1 is a valid chance baseline for selection that needs no extra runs.
The clean-label case is tested and reported, including that every drop there removes a correct sample and that a non-significant difference does not show equivalence.
Fig. 1 puts the pipeline, the composition of the drops and the paired gains with per-seed dots in one view, and a reader can see where the gain is small or unstable.

weaknesses.issue: The accuracy gain cannot be attributed to removing label errors, or to the out-of-fold design. There is no random-drop, oracle, in-sample filter or regularization control, and no other noise treatment. Removing samples at fixed C also changes the training-set size and the relative regularization. Sec. 4 nevertheless says the logistic regression comparison is 'The only comparison that isolates filtering', which the limitations paragraph contradicts. The motivation in Sec. 3 ('cannot have memorized a wrong label') and the first sentence of Sec. 5 present the out-of-fold check as what makes the filter work, and this was never compared with an in-sample check.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 3, 'Out-of-fold check'; Sec. 4, 'Methods'; Sec. 4.2, first paragraph; Sec. 5, first sentence and limitations
weaknesses.suggestion: Replace 'isolates filtering' with wording such as 'differs from ours only in the filtering step and its consequences (fewer samples, stronger relative regularization)'. Call the gain that of the whole drop-and-refit step wherever it is reported. Mark the memorization argument as a design motivation that was not tested, and open Sec. 5 with 'On these two datasets' in place of the general statement about small training sets.

weaknesses.issue: The verdicts rest on an uncorrected paired t-test over 5 overlapping re-splits that the paper itself says gives p-values that are likely too low, yet differences are still called 'established'. The caution is also applied unevenly: only the gaps to the clean-label reference are read as tentative. 'Both gaps at the higher rate pass it too' does not survive a correction: under Holm over the four gap tests none is rejected, because the smallest p (0.016) exceeds 0.05/4. The three significant gains over logistic regression do survive Holm over the four gain tests.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4, 'Statistics'; Sec. 4.2, first and second paragraphs; abstract; third contribution
weaknesses.suggestion: Use one corrected test for all comparisons, for example the Nadeau-Bengio corrected resampled t-test, which needs only the per-seed differences and the split sizes. My rough calculation from the listed p-values and effect sizes is that the three gains stay below 0.05 and none of the four clean-reference gaps does (please verify with a recipe). Report that, drop the word 'established' in favor of naming the test, and support the claim that ours stays below the reference with per-run counts (from results/runs.jsonl I count it below in 19 of 20 noisy runs and tied in 1).

weaknesses.issue: Table 1 is much wider than its column and runs into the right margin and line-number area (main.log reports an overfull box of about 55 pt). This breaks the venue format and is visible at first glance.
weaknesses.suggestion: Use a two-level header ('Digits' and 'Breast cancer' over '20%' and '40%' with cmidrule), which fits one column and also removes the shortened name 'Breast'. Apply the same header to Table 2.

weaknesses.issue: The contribution over classification filtering is thin and its boundary is unclear. By the paper's own summary, Brodley and Friedl already studied a single-algorithm filter and the trade-off between good data discarded and bad data retained, which are close to 'Correct dropped' and 'Left in kept set'. The evidence here is two small datasets, one noise type and no competing method, so it is hard to say what a reader learns that was not expected. The first contribution bullet is only the sum of the other two.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 1, contribution list; Sec. 2, 'Filtering mislabeled samples'
weaknesses.suggestion: State in Sec. 2 which measured quantities overlap with Brodley and Friedl and which are added (for example the share of lost accuracy won back and the per-seed spread, if that is the difference). Merge or replace the first bullet with a concrete finding, such as the weak case on breast cancer at the higher rate.

weaknesses.issue: 'Much of the lost accuracy returns' is extended to breast cancer at the lower rate, where the same paragraph says the gain is not established and the per-seed share ranges from -67% to 100%. A seed-mean ratio with that spread and a non-significant numerator does not support 'much returns'. The recorded half-recovery tests (stats.md) also find more than half recovered only on digits at the lower rate.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4.2, 'How much returns differs by setting'
weaknesses.suggestion: Limit the statement to seed means on digits, and say for breast cancer at the lower rate that the mean share is high but the data do not determine it.

weaknesses.issue: The weak-case paragraph explains the wrong quantity. It links the two least accurate seeds to more flips and noisier kept sets, but those seeds are least accurate for both methods, so this says nothing about why little of the loss returns. By my calculation from results/runs.jsonl, the share won back at the higher rate is low in all five seeds (about 9% to 35%), and the seed with the most flipped labels has the largest paired gain (5.8 points).
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4.2, 'Breast cancer at the higher rate is the weak case'; end of the Table 1 caption
weaknesses.suggestion: Replace the two-seed association with the per-seed range of the share won back (add a recipe), which shows that the weak recovery holds in every seed. Remove the sentence on flipped shares of the two seeds from the Table 1 caption, since the table does not show those values.

weaknesses.issue: The smaller factor between drop precision and flipped share at the higher rate is not evidence of a cost. Precision is at most 100%, so the factor is capped near 2.6 at the higher rate, below the factors observed at the lower rate (about 3.3 and 4.0); it had to fall. The paragraph also omits that drop precision itself rises with noise on digits (64.6% to 76.1%) while it falls on breast cancer.
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4.1, 'Heavier noise costs the filter on both sides', last sentence
weaknesses.suggestion: Delete the factor sentence. Say instead that recall falls and more correct samples are lost on both datasets, while drop precision moves in opposite directions on the two.

weaknesses.issue: Table 1 gives seed means only, although the per-seed spread matters for the weak case and for the share won back. A reader cannot judge any removal quantity or recovery figure from the table.
weaknesses.suggestion: Add sd to each removal quantity and the per-seed range for 'Won back' (all computable from results/runs.jsonl). A transposed layout or a second line per cell keeps it within one column.

weaknesses.issue: The MLP heading claims that a larger model does not make filtering unnecessary, while the paragraph under it says the gap says nothing about filtering or about larger models. One untuned MLP that loses to unfiltered logistic regression cannot support the heading. The paragraph also leaves out that on clean digits the MLP is significantly more accurate than ours (p = 0.031 in stats.md).
weaknesses.where: Sec. 4.2, 'A larger model does not make filtering unnecessary here'; Sec. 4, 'Methods'
weaknesses.suggestion: Retitle to the finding, for example 'The untuned MLP loses more to noise than logistic regression', or cut the paragraph to one sentence and use the space for the missing setup details. Remove the question about filtering being unnecessary from the setup.

weaknesses.issue: A reader cannot tell what is being classified. The feature vectors are never described (image pixels for digits, computed measurements for breast cancer), the number of digit classes is not given although the noise discussion depends on it, and the penalty of the logistic regression is left implicit.
weaknesses.suggestion: Add one sentence per dataset on the input features, say there are ten digit classes, and say that the penalty is the scikit-learn default.

weaknesses.issue: The schematic in Fig. 1a drops every mislabeled point and ends in a perfectly separated set. The data show survivors in every noisy setting, in large share on breast cancer at the higher rate.
weaknesses.suggestion: Leave one wrong label uncrossed and still present in the refit panel, and say in the caption that some mislabeled samples survive.

weaknesses.issue: Naming is inconsistent: 'ours', 'the filter', 'Filter (ours)' and 'the refit model' refer to overlapping things, and 'ours' sits oddly with 'We claim no new method'. Sentences such as 'Ours has a higher mean accuracy' and 'the test accuracy of ours minus that of logistic regression' are hard to read.
weaknesses.suggestion: Use 'the filter' for the selection step and one name, such as 'filtered logistic regression', for the refit model in text, figure legend and table.

weaknesses.issue: The 'Statistics' paragraph opens with a sentence on a writing and checking pipeline that says nothing about the statistics. The cited software entry carries personal names and a repository link, which may conflict with anonymous review.
weaknesses.suggestion: Remove the sentence and reference from the review version and use the space to describe the test.

questions: Does the filter drop one class more often than another, in particular on breast cancer under noise? If per-class drops were not saved, can this be listed as a limitation, since accuracy alone would not show it?
Did any logistic regression or MLP fit stop at its iteration limit? The setup gives the limits but not whether they were reached.
Given that the p-values are described as likely too low, what should a reader take 'established' to mean?
What does the MLP row tell a reader about the filter that the two logistic regression rows do not?
